subject.title: feat: render inline web chat widgets via capability-gated show_widget tool

question: Should OpenClaw accept `requiredClientCaps` as a plugin-visible tool API and ship Canvas `show_widget` as a bundled web-chat surface that executes self-contained model-authored markup inside an opaque sandbox?
rationale: The implementation is coherent but creates both a durable plugin API and a security-sensitive HTML/script rendering surface, so code review cannot safely decide the long-term product/security boundary alone.

options.title: Accept After Repair
options.body: Fix the pruning, type, and boundary defects, then land the generic capability seam and Canvas widget surface with maintainer approval and green proof.

options.title: Narrow The API
options.body: Keep the widget idea but hide or redesign the capability contract until maintainers are ready to expose a plugin-visible availability API.

options.title: Pause Bundled Widgets
options.body: Defer this bundled feature if maintainers want inline widgets to remain a ClawHub/plugin experiment for now.

recommendation.title: Accept After Repair
recommendation.body: Fix the pruning, type, and boundary defects, then land the generic capability seam and Canvas widget surface with maintainer approval and green proof.

likelyOwner.reason: He is tied to this PR and recent adjacent plugin/UI work, and is the clearest owner for the API and sandbox acceptance decision.
